text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Government's new Committee on Singapore's Competitiveness will consider "wide-ranging" measures to chart strategic direction for country's economic growth.
- Cathay Pacific Airways and sister carrier Dragonair cancel 24 flights on Tuesday, as problems with their Airbus 330-300s' Trent engines continue into fourth day.
- Hongkong parents, irked by cost of buying Japan's latest toy craze, have been joined by teachers, who have started to ban Tamagotch from classrooms.

- DBS Land buys Hospital Pantai's 19.16 percent stake in Singapore-listed health care group Parkway Holdings for Singapore $391.2 million in cash, saying the investment will position it as a major regional health care player.
- AT&T Corp in midst of merger talks with SBC Communications Corp, seeking to fashion deal that could be worth at least US$50 billion.
- China poised to allow establishment of second fixed-line telephone network, giving foreign investors first crack at one of world's fastest-growing markets.
- High Certificate of Entitlement (COE) premiums are taking a toll on parallel importers, some of whom have cars stuck at port awaiting delivery for lack of COEs.
- Hotel Grand Central has tied up with United Overseas Bank for unusual loan-cum-warrant deal that will also give the bank bond call options.
- Singapore Telecom expected to announce on Friday an unexciting net profit growth of 12-14 percent to Singapore $1.66-$1.7 billion.
- Listed transport company Comfort Group has taken its motor business abroad. Comfort Eurobike, its Piaggio scooter agency, has landed franchise in Brunei.
- Freight Links Express Holdings reports at S$3.67 milion net profit for nine months ended January 31.
- Tibs Taxis raising booking surcharge for premier service -- first cab company to do so after Public Transport Council's decision last month to deregulate the market.
